claims.says: the example boots and deploys locally
tf-check fails an unformatted root and names the file
only the roots a change touches are planned
one note groups many plans
the report is JSON and HTML, and links every root to its full plan
destroys and outliers are open, identical groups are folded
each wave goes out only once approved
a wave whose plans changed after approval applies nothing
a wave counts only an approval sealed by a key the signers file lists
drift is reported by root
a module version rolls out one pull request per wave
changed modules are published at a new version
tips are on by default and name their rule
with no more than a drift schedule and the canary wave in terragucci.yml, init writes the same pipeline
two pushes to main apply one after the other, and the commit carries one terragucci/apply status
a control repo opens one pull request per project that changes, and the merged pipeline applies
each plan run is one trace, with a span per root and the binary spans inside it
the metrics of a plan run reach Prometheus with the counts in its report
init finds Terragrunt and its 15 units on its own and writes the pipeline the Terragrunt example commits
the Terragrunt example boots, applying the canary wave before the rest with one run --all each
tf-check fails an unformatted Terragrunt file and names it
only the units a change reaches are planned, including a file a module reads that Terragrunt misses
a dependency whose mock_outputs can stand in for apply is named by a tip
a unit whose plan would read mock_outputs is not planned; it waits for its upstream to apply
a new upstream and its dependent merge together and apply in order, so no mock reaches real state
drift is reported by unit in a Terragrunt repo, with the same tracking issue
a refused wave names each root whose plan moved and the attributes that moved
a failed apply is triaged from the known-error table
drift on a literal becomes a pull request with the live value, and import blocks for what is unmanaged
each tip becomes its own small pull request
fmt on request commits to the pull request branch and nowhere else
release notes come from the conventional commits that touched the module
on a fresh estate the plan job holds back a root whose upstream is unapplied, names it in the report, and stays green
a Forgejo job gets an OIDC token Forgejo signed for its repo and ref, and trades it for the plan or apply role
